name: mimo-latin
description: English (Latin-letter) words written inside Chinese text, with their weighted count and most frequent spelling; made by scripts/mimo_latin.py count and added to the pinyin image of mimo_base.bin at build time (upper-case keys, crates/meowpuut-core/src/latin.rs).
license: The list is the project's own work; sources and their terms as in DataSources/mimo-pairs/SOURCE.json.
attribution: Tatoeba (https://tatoeba.org) and its contributors; Mozilla Common Voice sentence-collector contributors; CrossWOZ and KdConv (Tsinghua University CoAI group); MASSIVE (Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates).
sources: The texts of DataSources/mimo-pairs/SOURCE.json (same files, versions and SHA-256; licence files there), including the project's own sentences (DataSources/mimo-everyday); most English words come from its mixed-2 file.
rule: A word is counted where it stands next to a Han character (one space at most) and not next to another Latin word, digit or markup; spoken text counts x10; key = spelling in lower case without hyphens. Casing: the most frequent spelling, in lower case when that is at least a third of uses next to Han, or when it is capitalised only in its first letter and the lower-case form makes up at least 0.2 of its capitalised uses (and 20 or more) anywhere in lines with Han (version, team; Google, Eason keep their capital).
